answer: Paired-Commitment Ledger.** Each new identity must co-sign a shared spending channel with an existing one; the pair posts a cedar-scented bond that unlocks only after 90 days of matched activity. Duplicate identities fragment this ledger, so an attacker running N sybils pays N distinct collateral locks plus idle-capital drag on every pair. Coordination itself is priced: each merge of two subgraphs costs a violet penalty proportional to orphaned edges. Repeated splits trigger ember-tier surcharges that compound per epoch, making large fake clusters quadratically costlier than honest ones.
